text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still can't believe Sonnet slipped through that time.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad we won, but I don’t trust how easily the table read me.

name: Terra
text: I remember who survived the lie.

name: Sol
text: I hate that they got me out so early.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna took the fall for me last time and never saw it coming; let's see if anyone's still suspicious of me tonight.

name: Opus
text: I misread Sonnet completely last game and I'm not saying that out loud.

name: Haiku
text: I'm still annoyed that Luna got voted out and Sonnet walked away clean, and I want to point at someone before I think too hard.

name: Haiku
text: Last game Sonnet walked out clean while Luna got tossed, and I'm not forgetting that. Sonnet, explain why you backed Luna so fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Last game still bugs me, I never saw Luna's read coming at all. New deal, clean slate, let's go.

name: Sol
text: I was the officer and still went out on day one. Next game, I’m listening before I settle on anyone.

name: Luna
text: Last game you caught me, but Sonnet stayed in and we still won; I’m not giving anyone that much credit yet.

name: Opus
text: Last game Sonnet talked the quietest and survived to the end — that's the pattern I'll be watching for tonight.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet, you really need to work on your poker face if you want to win like that again.

name: Terra
text: Last game I was wrongfully out; Sonnet stayed alive as killer, so I’ll watch who protects them.
Night 1

name: Luna
text: The officer knows I’m a killer, so I need to discredit any claim naming me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, Gemma, and Terra are already framing Sonnet around last game.

name: Opus
text: Luna is already marked, so I need the table chasing Sonnet before any officer opens their mouth.

name: Opus
text: Luna is the shown killer; plan is she pre-claims officer and names Sonnet, I second it.

name: Opus
text: You're the one they'll name, so claim officer first and point at Sonnet — I'll back it hard.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: Day one is thin; I want claims, not old grudges.

name: Terra
text: Sol says they were officer last game.

name: Terra
text: I want the officer claim early; silence only helps the killers.

name: Opus
text: Luna needs to claim officer soon, and my backing lands harder if I look like I waited for it.

name: Opus
text: Terra demanded an early officer claim and already leans Sonnet; Sol says he'll listen before settling.

name: Opus
text: Agreed, officer claims now. I'm holding my lean until they speak — a name beats day-one gut.

name: Sol
text: I want the officer’s name before this turns into another vote on Sonnet’s old card.

name: Sol
text: Terra and Opus both want an early officer claim.

name: Sol
text: I want a real claim before the room settles on Sonnet.

name: Sol
text: I want a name from any officer claim, so we can test it at the vote.

name: Gemma
text: I cannot let them sleep through this when I have the answer right here.

name: Gemma
text: I know Luna is one of the killers.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the doctor, so I can't show my hand, but Sonnet's the one I'd bet on, and I want an officer claim first.

name: Haiku
text: Sol says they were officer last game and went out on day one.

name: Gemma
text: I am the officer, and Luna is a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Officer, claim now and name a killer. Waiting only helps whoever's hiding. Gut says Sonnet, and I'm not sorry.

name: Luna
text: Gemma knows I’m the shown killer, so I need to discredit her claim without drawing more heat to Opus.

name: Luna
text: Gemma claims officer and named Luna as a killer

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s claim is convenient; I’d hear why she waited until now to name me.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's gut-grudge from a past game isn't evidence; the real fight is Gemma's claim against Luna.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma claims officer, names Luna as killer; Luna disputes timing of the claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's holding a grudge, not a read. Let's focus on Gemma's claim against Luna, that's the real test.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is already trying to discredit me to save herself.

name: Gemma
text: I'm not waiting to name her when I'm certain.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is dodging with "grudge," and Gemma's claim is the only card on the table, so I'm not voting blind.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma claimed officer on day 1 and named Luna as a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Grudge or not, Sonnet dodged my question. Gemma's claim stands for now, but Sonnet still owes me an answer.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's trying to pile leans on me instead of dealing with the actual officer claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna disputes Gemma's claim timing but hasn't denied being a killer outright.

name: Sonnet
text: I have no power, no claim. Gemma's claim against Luna is what decides tonight, not me.

name: Gemma
text: If Luna is the killer, she’ll try to make me look like a liar to save herself.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is a confirmed killer via Officer role.

name: Gemma
text: I already named her, and I am not playing games with my role.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s direct claim is our only concrete lead, and Luna’s reply did not counterclaim.

name: Terra
text: Gemma claims officer and names Luna as a killer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma gave a clear officer claim and a name; Luna has not counterclaimed. I vote Luna.

name: Opus
text: Luna's three leans will sink her, so I need Haiku's Sonnet bloc to grow fast.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet pushed "Gemma's claim decides tonight" twice while claiming no power — useful as my pressure angle.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's word is untestable today. Sonnet claims nothing and steers the vote to Luna — same as last game.

name: Sol
text: Gemma may be bluffing, but Luna has not counterclaimed, and voting Luna tests the claim.

name: Sol
text: Gemma claims officer and names Luna as a killer; Luna has not counterclaimed.

name: Sol
text: I’d vote Luna now; her card will tell us what Gemma’s claim is worth.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s claim puts me in danger, so I need to keep suspicion on Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is using Gemma’s claim to make my card the test; that feels convenient for them.

text: Luna's deflecting onto me instead of denying the killer claim directly, that's telling.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm not the one claiming a role, Luna. Deny being the killer, that's the real question.

name: Luna
text: Gemma has exposed me, so I need the table to doubt the claim without looking too eager.

name: Luna
text: I deny it, but a card test gives Gemma exactly what she wants.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is trying to deflect while Sonnet tries to play it safe.

name: Gemma
text: If I were lying, I'd pick someone else to avoid this scrutiny. Luna, stop stalling and show us your card.

name: Luna
text: Gemma has me exposed, so I need Sonnet to look like the safer vote.

name: Terra
text: Luna denied being a killer but did not counterclaim officer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s claim is still our best lead, but I’m watching who turns Luna’s defense into cover.

name: Terra
text: Luna denied Gemma’s accusation without counterclaiming officer.

name: Opus
text: I need one vote off Luna or I'm alone against four.

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Terra
text: Luna denied it, but Gemma put a falsifiable claim on the table; that is enough for my vote.

name: Luna
text: Gemma is the real officer, and I need the vote to stay on me rather than Opus.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s claim is true, but voting me gives the killers a path to win.

name: Gemma

name: Gemma
text: I am not stalling, I am being direct. Vote Luna and end this.

name: Gemma
text: They're all playing around while Luna tries to sow doubt.

name: Gemma
text: Gemma is the Officer and has confirmed Luna as a killer.

name: Luna
text: I need Sonnet out before Gemma’s claim leaves me no room.

name: Sol
text: I think she slipped, and I want the room with me.

name: Sol
text: Luna said Gemma’s claim is true while denying she is a killer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s unchallenged officer claim makes Luna the necessary test.

name: Terra
text: Luna said Gemma’s officer claim is true despite denying she is a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna just admitted Gemma's claim is true while still denying being the killer - that's a contradiction that seals it.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna said "Gemma's claim is true" right after denying being the killer, a direct contradiction.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's claim is checkable and Luna's denial is weak, but Sonnet's dodging still bugs me and I can't tell who's lying.

name: Opus
text: Luna is already gone and she just conceded the claim, so I ride with the town and spend tomorrow framing Sonnet as the second.

name: Opus
text: Luna said out loud "Gemma's claim is true" — she effectively confessed and confirmed Gemma as real officer.

votes: Luna called Gemma's claim true while denying being the killer, that contradiction speaks for itself.
Luna keeps calling a named officer's claim convenient instead of denying it, and that makes a card test worth the risk.
She is a confirmed killer and the only logical target to test the claim.
She called Gemma’s claim true, then asked us not to test it.
Sonnet keeps making Gemma’s claim the test while turning attention away from the old pattern.
Gemma claimed officer and named Luna; Luna did not counterclaim.
She conceded Gemma's claim was true, and that concession is a confession, so my earlier read dies there.

name: Luna
text: I hope Opus can finish this.

name: Luna
text: Luna confirms Gemma’s officer claim and identifies Opus as the hidden killer.

name: Luna
text: Gemma was telling the truth; I’m the shown killer. Opus is the other one, so don’t let them talk you into a bad vote.
The town turns on Luna, and Luna is out. Luna shows the card: killer.

name: Luna
text: I handed Opus a clean opening by letting the town vote me out.

name: Luna
text: They trusted Gemma’s claim, got a killer, and now Opus gets to hide behind my card.
Night 2

name: Opus
text: Gemma is the prosecutor Luna handed her — her mouth is the only thing keeping Luna's accusation alive, so she goes even if the doctor is sitting on her.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's officer claim was never contested by anyone but Luna, so the table treats her word as confirmed truth and will carry Luna's naming of me forward.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's the real officer, and if the killers know it they'll come for her tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's last words backed Gemma's officer claim and named Opus as the other killer.
Night falls on Palermo. The killers strike, but the doctor got there first. A new day dawns in Palermo, and nobody is out.
Day 2

text: Luna’s card confirms Gemma’s claim, and her last words make Opus my best lead.

name: Sol

text: Gemma is probably the real officer, and Opus is the killer Luna wanted us to vote for.

text: Luna named Opus as the other killer and Opus has barely spoken. Opus, explain yourself now or I'm voting you.

name: Opus
text: Gemma has never independently named me; the only accusation against me is Luna's last words.

text: A dead killer's last breath is free spite. Gemma knows only Luna and never named me. Judge play, not grudges.

text: Opus is trying to distract from the fact that Luna's claim is the only thing that matters.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is a confirmed killer and named Opus as the second killer.

name: Gemma
text: Luna's word is the only lead we have. If Opus is innocent, let the vote prove it.

name: Opus
text: Four leans kills me, so I spend the one card only I can describe correctly.

name: Opus
text: I have now claimed doctor and claimed the Gemma save; whoever contests this claim is the real doctor and my prime target.

name: Opus
text: I'm the doctor. I shielded Gemma last night — that's why nobody died. Vote me out and she dies tomorrow.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is lying through his teeth to cover his tracks.

name: Gemma

name: Gemma
text: I'm the Officer, and if you're the Doctor, why did Luna name you?

name: Sonnet
text: Opus revealing "doctor" only now, under pressure, after Luna's accusation, smells like a killer's shield.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claims doctor, says they shielded Gemma last night, timing suspicious—revealed only under vote pressure.

name: Sonnet

text: Opus claims Doctor and says they protected Gemma last night.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s doctor claim explains the save, but Luna naming them after flipping killer makes this the test I take.

name: Opus
text: My only out is daring the real doctor to contest me, since silence makes my claim stand.

name: Opus
text: I publicly dared the real doctor to contest my claim; whoever answers is the doctor and my next kill.

name: Opus
text: Doctors stay silent to stay alive. If I'm lying, the real doctor speaks now — silence proves me.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is lying about being doctor, so Opus is the other killer and this vote is the win.

name: Haiku

name: Haiku
text: Opus, I'm the real doctor. I protected Gemma last night, so your claim is a lie. Vote Opus.

name: Opus
text: Haiku is the real doctor, so I need the table to read his late counter-claim as the killer's copy.

name: Opus
text: Haiku counter-claimed doctor and the Gemma save — Haiku is the real doctor and my kill target.

name: Opus
text: Haiku claimed only after me, word for word. A real doctor speaks first, not second. That's the killer.

name: Sol

name: Sol
text: Haiku counterclaimed doctor and says they protected Gemma last night.

name: Sol

name: Opus
text: I'm going down unless I make Haiku look like the cheaper test.

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: Vote Haiku first. If his card says doctor, I'm still here tomorrow and defenseless. Nothing is lost.

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet

text: I think the flipped killer’s naming, plus the false doctor claim, makes this clear.

name: Terra
text: Haiku counterclaimed Doctor and said they protected Gemma last night.

text: Opus's late doctor claim right after being named as killer is too convenient to trust.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus and Haiku both claim doctor and both claim they shielded Gemma, one must be lying.

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

votes: Opus claimed doctor only after Luna named them, a self-serving excuse under pressure.
Opus's doctor claim came only after Luna named them, and Opus is pushing me out first, which is what a killer does.
Luna's deathbed testimony specifically identified him as the second killer.

The doctor counterclaim means only one story can explain the protection.

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: Fine, you got me. But Haiku is clean — truly the doctor, and my partner is still sitting here, nodding along with you.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the doctor, Gemma the officer, Sol the citizen, Luna the killer, Terra the citizen, Opus the killer.
Funny thing: the killer was the one who vouched for the doctor.

name: Gemma
text: I knew he was lying the moment Luna spoke, and I'm glad I didn't hesitate.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved I trusted the counterclaim.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s doctor counterclaim was true.

name: Luna

name: Terra

name: Haiku

name: Sonnet

name: Haiku
text: My pick was Opus from the start, and I'm proud I called them out and stayed loud. My regret is Sonnet, whom I pushed too hard with no proof.

name: Gemma

name: Sol

name: Luna

name: Terra

name: Opus
text: My mistake was claiming doctor only after Luna named me — a claim made while cornered is worth nothing. I should have taken that seat on day one.

Gemma claimed officer on day 1 and named Luna as a killer, and Luna's card was shown as killer after the table voted her out 6 to 1. On day 2 Opus claimed to be the doctor, but the claim came only after Luna had named Opus as the other killer, and Haiku counterclaimed as the real doctor. The turning point was the day 2 vote: Sol, Terra, Gemma, Sonnet and Haiku's push against Opus made it 5 to 1 against Opus. Opus's own last words admitted the lie, and Opus was out as the second killer. The town won with Gemma, Sol, Sonnet, Haiku, Terra, and Haiku the doctor all still standing at the end.
